Claims remain bounded to current IRS retrieval routes, transcript-type descriptions, availability limits, privacy safeguards, April 2025 Form 4506-T revision, and the transcript-versus-return-copy distinction.

The article invents no taxpayer, tax year, return, transcript entry, mineral interest, property, payer, offer, basis, income character, calculation, form selection, filing, retention period, or professional conclusion.

sources_inspected.label: IRS, Get your tax records and transcripts (accessed 2026-08-26)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current IRS Get your tax records and transcripts page supplies official online-account, mail, and automated-phone retrieval routes, the five-to-ten-calendar-day mail estimate, address-of-record boundary, masking notice, and link to Form 4506-T.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: It supports retrieval-channel and handoff documentation only. It does not select a transcript, prove mineral ownership or basis, establish completeness, characterize income, calculate tax, validate an offer, or recommend a transaction.

sources_inspected.label: IRS, Transcript types for individuals and ways to order them (accessed 2026-08-26)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current IRS transcript-types page defines the limited contents and stated availability of return, account, record-of-account, wage-and-income, and verification-of-non-filing records and identifies the routes through which they may be requested.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: It supports a source-scope matrix and neutral availability notes only. The article does not decide which transcript an owner needs, interpret an entry, treat missing data as negative proof, or convert a tax record into title, basis, offer, or transaction evidence.

sources_inspected.label: IRS, About tax transcripts (accessed 2026-08-26)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current IRS About tax transcripts page supplies the masking, fully visible financial-entry, customer-file-number, no-IRS-fax, and no-third-party-mailing boundaries.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: It supports privacy cautions, unaltered-copy handling, and secure professional handoff only. It does not establish that a transmission method is universally secure or authorize public exposure of taxpayer information.

sources_inspected.label: IRS, About Form 4506-T (accessed 2026-08-26)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current IRS About Form 4506-T page identifies the form as the official paper request route for listed transcript types and links to the current revision.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: It supports a current-source pointer only. The article does not complete the form, choose a request, supply an address, authorize a signer, or provide owner-specific filing instructions.

sources_inspected.label: IRS, Form 4506-T, revision April 2025 (accessed 2026-08-26)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The official Form 4506-T PDF is revision April 2025 and supplies IRS-stated transcript descriptions, availability notes, processing statements, signature timing, and the instruction to consult the official landing page for developments.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: It supports a revision-control and professional-review boundary only. The article does not reproduce the form, fill a field, select a transcript or year, decide authority to sign, state a mailing destination, or promise processing time.

sources_inspected.label: IRS, Topic 156, transcript or copy of a tax return (accessed 2026-08-26)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: IRS Topic 156 distinguishes a transcript from a complete return copy, identifies Form 4506-T as a mail route for transcript types, and identifies Form 4506 as the separate route for a complete return copy.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: It supports the transcript-versus-copy boundary only. The article does not recommend ordering a paid copy, state a current copy fee, or decide which record an owner or CPA requires.
